audit-surfaces.title: Where Copilot evidence lives
audit-surfaces.description: Copilot evidence sits in separate layers: the audit log for settings and agent actions, the agent sessions view, usage records and client-side telemetry, each owned and retained differently.

access-methods.title: Four ways to read the audit log
access-methods.description: Compare the web view, export, REST API and streaming by time range, API request events and Git events before choosing how to collect Copilot audit evidence.

plan-policy-events.title: Copilot event families
plan-policy-events.description: Group Copilot audit events into seat changes, policy and settings changes, content and memory changes, plan and terms changes and access changes, then search each by action prefix.

agent-audit-fields.title: Read an agent audit record
agent-audit-fields.description: An agent audit record pairs the action with actor_is_agent, agent_session_id and the initiating user, and links to the commit co-author and session log for context.

agent-session-view.title: From session view to audit log
agent-session-view.description: Open AI controls, review recent agent sessions, open the 24-hour list, filter it, then move to the audit log with actor:Copilot for anything older or more detailed.

usage-records-stream.title: Turn on usage records
usage-records-stream.description: Check eligibility, enable the Copilot usage records streaming policy and send records to a destination, or read them with the usage records API instead.

retention-windows.title: How long each record lasts
retention-windows.description: Compare retention: the agent sessions list covers 24 hours, Git events 7 days, the audit log 180 days, and a stream keeps whatever your destination keeps from the day you enable it.

stream-operations.title: Keep a stream healthy
stream-operations.description: A paused stream buffers up to seven days, resumes from a week earlier after longer pauses and needs a new stream after three weeks; run the health check and fix failures within six days.

investigation-playbook.title: Five steps to a bounded finding
investigation-playbook.description: Scope the question, triage with the audit log, collect from each source in its window, attribute actions to users and agents, then write a bounded conclusion.

alert-design.title: Design an alert you can act on
alert-design.description: Each alert pairs a signal with a precise match condition and a named owner response, so a firing alert leads to a check rather than a guess.

otel-correlation.title: Join telemetry to the audit log
otel-correlation.description: Client OpenTelemetry nests chat and tool spans under an invoke_agent root; join them to audit records on identity and time, since matching conversation and session IDs is not documented.

evidence-limits.title: What each record proves
evidence-limits.description: For each source, separate what the record shows from what it does not show, so findings stay within the evidence.
